lmms-eval (vendored)
====================
upstream:  https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval
version:   0.5.0 (pyproject.toml)
copied at: 2026-08-21
copied from: OneVision-Encoder/llava_next/lmms-eval
             (OneVision-Encoder commit cdc7456df059801226bc075398ab24b09822a4aa)

This directory is a snapshot of upstream third-party code. Do not modify it by
hand except for the local changes listed below, so that it can be diffed/merged
against upstream in the future.

Local changes (five):
  1. lmms_eval/models/__init__.py
     Added one entry to AVAILABLE_SIMPLE_MODELS:
       "llava_covisco": "LlavaCoVisco"
  2. lmms_eval/models/simple/llava_covisco.py  (new file in this repo)
     Evaluation adapter for CoVisco + Qwen3.
  3. pyproject.toml
     Upstream uses license = "MIT" + license-files = ["LICENSE"] (PEP 639),
     which requires setuptools>=77; with setuptools 75.8.0 in this environment
     the `project.license` validation fails, so it was changed to
     license = { text = "MIT" }. Revert to the upstream form after upgrading
     to setuptools>=77.
  4. lmms_eval/tasks/nextqa/stopwords.csv  (restored missing file)
     This file was dropped when the snapshot was copied, but tasks/nextqa/utils.py
     reads it at import time, causing the nextqa task to fail to load. Content is
     the nltk English stopword list.
  5. lmms_eval/tasks/mvbench/utils.py
     In mvbench_process_results, gt and candidates are now compared as strings,
     fixing a crash on the moving_count / action_count subtasks where answer was
     an int.

Install:
  pip install -e third_party/lmms-eval --no-deps --no-build-isolation
